summary: Minimal 630-line Python harness that runs an agent in a nightly loop — edit training script, time-box experiment, keep if metric improves, revert otherwise. Autonomous ML experimentation at ~100 runs per night.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AutoResearch is purpose-built for iterative ML training script optimization. AgentForge orchestrates software development against Linear issues, not ML model training; the fitness-signal loop concept doesn't map to our artifact-first state machine.

summary: AgentHub described as 'GitHub rebuilt for AI agents' — registry for discovering, sharing, and versioning agent definitions. 100% open source.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge is an orchestrator, not an agent registry. Interesting as ecosystem context but no concrete gap to address.

source: Mem0 State of AI Agent Memory 2026 Benchmark Report
summary: Comprehensive 2026 benchmark establishing episodic, semantic, and procedural memory taxonomy for agents. MAGMA achieves highest LoCoMo score (0.7). Standardized eval suite now exists for comparing memory architectures.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge already ships skill distillation + planner injection. Executor memory injection (HID-188) is the remaining open gap. The benchmark confirms the three-tier taxonomy matches AgentForge's existing split: skills=procedural, run outcomes=episodic, codebase context=semantic.

source: MAGMA: Multi-Graph based Agentic Memory Architecture (ACL 2026)
summary: Represents each memory item across orthogonal semantic, temporal, causal, and entity graphs; retrieval as policy-guided graph traversal. Outperforms flat-vector-similarity approaches on LoCoMo and LongMemEval benchmarks.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — Interesting extension beyond single-vector retrieval for skill memory, but requires graph infrastructure (new DB or graph layer) that is out of scope for 1-2 agent runs. HID-188 already tracks the open memory gap; MAGMA could inform a future enhancement of that issue once it ships.

source: Escher-Loop: Mutual Evolution by Closed-Loop Self-Referential Optimization (ICML 2026 AI4Math)
summary: Closed-loop framework where a Task Agent population and an Optimizer Agent population co-evolve: optimizers improve tasks, task results score optimizers. Achieves higher peak performance on math optimization problems (Kissing Number, Circle Packing) than static baselines.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — Targets mathematical optimization via evolutionary search. AgentForge runs deterministic CLI subprocesses against fixed Linear issues; there is no optimizer-vs-task population to co-evolve. Architecture is fundamentally incompatible with our sequential state machine.

summary: Open-source LangGraph-based super-agent harness with sandboxed execution, persistent memory, sub-agent delegation, extensible skills (built-in, MCP, community), and message gateway to Slack/Telegram/Feishu. Hit #1 on GitHub Trending Feb 2026 (~25k stars).
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — DeerFlow's skill system and sub-agent pattern are directionally similar to AgentForge's distillation pipeline. Key differences: DeerFlow uses Python/LangGraph while AgentForge uses TypeScript/Fastify with CLI subprocess agents. No specific gap in AgentForge closes by adopting DeerFlow patterns that isn't already tracked (HID-188 for skills, HID-72 for dispatch loop). Backlog is full; revisit if backlog drains.

summary: LangGraph 0.3.x shipped PostgresSaver checkpointer and a streaming tool-output API in Feb 2026. LangGraph surpassed CrewAI in GitHub stars, cementing enterprise dominance. Provides audit-trail-friendly state persistence for long-horizon agents.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses Prisma/PostgreSQL for run state already, not LangGraph. The PostgresSaver concept maps to our existing DB-backed stage model. Streaming tool output is already shipped via SSE (runEventEmitter.ts). No open gap this addresses that isn't tracked.

summary: AutoGen v1.0 GA (Feb 2026) stabilizes the v2 API; leads in research/academic multi-agent debate and verification patterns. Strong for parallel multi-agent panels; trails on production error recovery.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AutoGen's multi-agent debate pattern was explicitly evaluated and rejected for AgentForge (cost multiplier per architecture notes). HID-93 tracks adversarial plan critique via a lighter mechanism. Nothing new from this release changes that calculus.

summary: Curated survey of self-evolving agent papers, benchmarks, and open-source projects. Documents patterns: closed-loop feedback from judge/test suite, atomic skill acquisition via reusable modules, experience persistence (Lessons Learned + Workflow Templates), recursive meta-reasoning.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — The 'atomic skill acquisition + experience persistence' pattern directly matches AgentForge's distillation pipeline. Recursive meta-reasoning and Lessons Learned structures could inform how distilled skills are structured in agentSkillRepository.ts, but this is an incremental improvement to existing shipped code, not a new capability gap. No open gap beyond HID-188.

source: Jim Fan NVIDIA ENPIRE (fleet robotics + compute)
summary: Jim Fan's recent NVIDIA work focuses on ENPIRE — giving Codex agents a fleet of robots and compute resources for task-parallel execution while maintaining safety. Continued focus on physical AGI via Project GR00T.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — ENPIRE targets robotic fleet coordination. AgentForge orchestrates software development subprocesses, not robotic hardware. No transfer of concepts at the implementation level.

source: Shunyu Yao — moved to Tencent as Chief AI Scientist
summary: Shunyu Yao (ReAct, Tree of Thoughts) left OpenAI to become Tencent's Chief AI Scientist. No specific new 2026 agent architecture paper found; foundational ReAct/ToT work continues to be widely cited and embedded in frameworks.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — No new actionable methodology from Yao in 2026 yet. ReAct is already the implicit pattern in AgentForge's agent-thought sections within promptRenderer.ts.

summary: Harrison Chase introduced 'Deep Agents' at ODSC AI West 2025 — long-horizon agent harness with planning, subagents, filesystem, and self-structured memory. 2026 vision: memory + tool use + evaluation + model behavior compound when tuned together.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — The 'compound improvement' thesis (memory + eval + orchestration) is the same thesis AgentForge is already executing on. Chase's emphasis on human-in-the-loop at approval gates mirrors AgentForge's AwaitingPlanApproval stage. No gap this surfaces that isn't tracked.
